issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Allow signed-in MapThru users to connect one Google account as an additional sign-in method from /profile → Password and Security, even when the Google email differs from the primary MapThru account email. Connecting Google must never merge accounts, move projects, or transfer billing/collaboration data.

Docs:

  • PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-connect-google-sso-account/prd.md
  • Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-connect-google-sso-account/brief.md

RESULT

Branch: design/connect-google-SSO-account

Problem

Google login today is tied directly to the Google email address. Users with an existing MapThru account (email/password) risk creating a duplicate account, losing sight of their projects, or hitting a conflict if they try to sign in with Google using a different email than their MapThru account.

Solution

Add a Google sign-in method card to /profile under Password and Security:

  • Shows connection status (Connected / Not connected)
  • Shows primary MapThru email separately from the connected Google email
  • Connect Google action (OAuth) when not connected
  • Disconnect action when connected and password login is available
  • Guides the user to set a password first when disconnect would lock them out

Locked Decisions

  • Google email may differ from the MapThru account email; MapThru email stays primary.
  • One MapThru account ↔ one Google account (exclusive, both directions).
  • Conflicting Google connections are blocked, never merged.
  • Disconnect is only allowed when password login is available.

In Scope

  • Connect Google from signed-in Profile > Password and Security
  • Login with a connected Google account
  • Display connected Google status + email
  • Disconnect Google when password login available
  • Conflict / failure / lockout-prevention messaging
  • QA coverage: same-email and different-email flows

Out of Scope

  • Automatic account merge / project / billing transfer
  • Multiple Google accounts per MapThru account (or vice versa)
  • Account chooser during Google login
  • Changing the user's primary MapThru email
  • Separate Google SSO settings route (v1)

Acceptance Criteria

  • User can connect Google with the same email as their MapThru account
  • User can connect Google with a different email; MapThru email stays unchanged
  • Google login opens the previously-connected MapThru account, never a duplicate
  • Connecting a Google account already linked to/representing another MapThru account is blocked with a neutral message
  • Disconnect is only available when hasPassword is true; otherwise the user is guided to set a password
  • Connect/disconnect loading, success, blocked, and failed states are all represented in the UI without exposing raw backend errors
  • Frontend refreshes account auth-method status after OAuth return and after disconnect
  • Long MapThru/Google emails truncate gracefully on mobile and desktop
  • All controls (connect, disconnect, confirm, cancel, retry, set password) are keyboard-reachable with visible focus states

Full functional requirements (GCA-R1–R20) and QA scenarios (21 scenarios) are in the PRD linked above.

Frontend Data Contract

Field Purpose
email Primary MapThru account email
hasPassword Whether password login is available
googleConnected Whether a Google account is connected
googleEmail Connected Google email, when available
canDisconnectGoogle Whether disconnect is safe without lockout

Error categories for UI mapping: conflict, verification_failed, already_connected, unsafe_disconnect, unauthenticated, generic_failure.

  • Google sign-in card implemented on /profile → Password and Security, covering all PRD states (not connected, connecting, connected same/different email, disconnect confirmation, disconnect blocked, success/error feedback) with keyboard/focus/aria-live handling.
  • Connect/disconnect currently run against a local mock (src/lib/googleAccount/connect.ts) — the Go API has no /v1/auth/google/link or /unlink endpoint yet. Flagged for Backend.
  • getMeAction extended with googleConnected / googleEmail, read defensively (defaults to false/null until the backend adds them).

issues.display_title: Issue #657: Wizard Mappedin: preserve imported buildings on Add More Floors (Main Building + per-building floor ordering)
issues.main_description_html:
Keep imported Mappedin buildings and floors grouped through the whole Create New Tour wizard, not just the import review modal. After Add More Floors, imported floors stay inside their imported buildings, any new manual/image floor goes to Main Building by default, and floor ordering happens inside each building group instead of one flat project-wide list.

PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-wizard-mappedin-add-more-floors-building-safety/prd.md
Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-wizard-mappedin-add-more-floors-building-safety/brief.md
Related PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-mappedin-import-building-grouping/prd.md (#643)

RESULT

Branch: design/wizard-mappedin

Problem

Mappedin imports can contain multiple buildings, and the review modal now groups them correctly. The risk starts one step later: when the user picks Add More Floors instead of going straight to the editor.

If the wizard treats everything after import as one flat list, imported floors lose their building context. Reordering then looks harmless but can silently move a floor into the wrong building — and a manually uploaded floor plan has no clear home, so it can appear to belong to an imported building by accident.

For malls, campuses, hospitals, and mixed-use venues that structure is the whole point of the import, so this turns into cleanup work right after the wizard.

Scope

  1. Add More Floors — imported buildings and per-floor building membership survive the jump into the upload step.
  2. Manual/image floors — default to Main Building, shown as a normal building group when it has floors.
  3. Floor ordering step — grouped by building for multi-building projects; reorder within a group only.
  4. Continue to Editor — the editor opens with exactly the structure the wizard showed.

Requirements

ID Requirement Priority
R1 After Mappedin import, Add More Floors preserves imported buildings. Must
R2 After Mappedin import, Add More Floors preserves each imported floor's building. Must
R3 New manual or image-based floors added after import belong to Main Building by default. Must
R4 Main Building is visible when it contains manually added floors in a multi-building wizard flow. Must
R5 The floor ordering step groups floors by building for multi-building projects. Must
R6 Users can reorder floors within a building group. Must
R7 Reordering floors does not move a floor from one building to another. Must
R8 Imported building names remain readable and user-facing. Must
R9 Missing building names use a simple fallback such as Building 1 or Main Building. Must
R10 The wizard clearly shows which floors are imported and which were manually added when needed for clarity. Should
R11 Continuing to the editor preserves imported buildings, Main Building, and floor order. Must
R12 Removing an imported floor removes only that floor and does not disturb other buildings. Must
R13 Removing a manual floor removes it from Main Building and does not disturb imported buildings. Must
R14 Single-building imports remain simple and do not require unnecessary building management. Must
R15 Existing image upload behavior remains unchanged for users who do not import from Mappedin. Must
R16 The UI avoids raw ids, source file names, and technical implementation language. Must

Out of scope

  • Moving floors between buildings inside the wizard.
  • A full building manager inside the wizard.
  • Renaming buildings or editing imported floor names inside the import review modal.
  • Guessing which imported building a manual floor belongs to.
  • Changing editor building management or the editor Add Floor import behavior (already preserves imported buildings — #643).
  • Billing, permissions, collaboration, publishing, live viewer, embed behavior.
  • New import formats.

Acceptance checklist

  • Add More Floors preserves imported Mappedin buildings.
  • Add More Floors preserves imported floor membership.
  • Manual/image floors added after import go to Main Building.
  • Main Building is visible when manual floors exist in a multi-building project.
  • Floor ordering is grouped by building for multi-building projects.
  • Users can reorder floors within a building group.
  • Reordering does not move floors between buildings.
  • Continue to Editor preserves imported buildings.
  • Continue to Editor preserves Main Building.
  • Continue to Editor preserves floor order within each building.
  • Removing floors does not disturb unrelated buildings.
  • Single-building imports remain simple.
  • Image-only wizard flows remain unchanged.
  • Copy is clear, plain, and non-technical.

Manual verification

  1. Start a new project.
  2. Import a Mappedin file with at least two buildings.
  3. Choose Add More Floors.
  4. Add one image floor manually.
  5. Continue to the floor ordering step.
  6. Confirm imported floors are grouped under their imported buildings.
  7. Confirm the manually added floor is grouped under Main Building.
  8. Reorder floors inside one imported building — confirm the floor stays in that building.
  9. Reorder the manual floor inside Main Building (if more than one manual floor exists).
  10. Continue to the editor and confirm the same building + floor structure.
  11. Repeat with a single-building import and confirm the flow stays simple.
  12. Repeat with an image-only flow (no Mappedin) and confirm nothing changed.
